Serenity@aleabitoreddit
19:04 SGTInvesting
Some industry commentary regarding a few claims recently on memory + Softbank Turbine defaulting.

- On claims that LTAs are "meaningless while prices fall":

$MU: "strategic customer agreements cannot be unilaterally canceled. Customers are obligated to pay for their committed volumes whether they take delivery or not"

"These are take or pay agreements and there are no contractual outs for our customers from these agreements"

Regarding historical contracts breaking: "These LTAs that we used to have never had any binding terms." The new SCAs contain extensive contractual obligations

Regarding Elon's claims on Softbank defaulting on Turbines:

Question from Morgan Stanley to $GE Vernova CEO on whether they see cancellations or financing difficulties with counterparties on their turbine orders:

“No… we are not”

TLDR:
- Micron states LTAs/SCAs are noncancellable take/pay (where counterparties are hyperscalers). And that these types are different from historical memory cancellations.

- On Softbank turbine orders, GE Vernova CEO Scott Strazik said it wasn't seeing customer financing disruptions, requests to exit turbine reservations, or slowdowns.

Maybe Elon's claims are more narrow, but should be evaluated more closely given competitive interests vs. Softbank/OpenAI.

Antonio Linares@alc2022
20:33 SGTInvesting
$HIMS just became a two-sided operating system for healthcare. Today, Eli Lilly signed a formal partnership to distribute Zepbound and Foundayo through the $HIMS platform. Earlier this year, Novo Nordisk did the same with Wegovy. The two companies that dominate obesity medicine now both supply through $HIMS.

This is the moment the flywheel grows a second side. Here's how it works:

1/ The supply side: pharma. Building a direct-to-consumer channel is slow, expensive and outside pharma's core skill. $HIMS already has the patients, the providers, the pharmacy logistics and the brand. Lilly plugs in and reaches millions of self-pay patients without building any of it. Lower cost to reach each patient means a higher return on every drug they've already spent billions developing.
2/ The demand side: patients. A patient opens one app and gets a consultation, a prescription if appropriate, and home delivery. Foundayo starts at $149/month and Zepbound at $299/month, branded and FDA-approved, with no compounded substitutes. More choice, lower friction, same price as anywhere else. Outcomes per dollar go up.
3/ The two sides feed each other. Every new pharma partner makes the platform more valuable to patients: wider catalog, better prices, more options for the provider to match to each person. Every new patient makes the platform more valuable to pharma: more reach, more demand, more real-world data on adherence and response.
4/ The data is where it compounds. Every consultation, every check-in, every lab panel, every switch from one therapy to another becomes longitudinal outcome data that no single drugmaker can collect on its own. Patients get treatment matched to them. Pharma learns what works, for whom, in the real world.
5/ This is why both sides improve outcomes per dollar at once. Pharma gets more outcome per R&D dollar because its drugs reach the right patients at a fraction of the distribution cost. Patients get more outcome per healthcare dollar because the platform matches them to the best intervention at the best price.
6/ Then the gravity flips. The more pharma supplies through $HIMS, the more patients come. The more patients come, the more pharma has to supply through $HIMS. Lilly and Novo are fierce competitors, and both just chose the same platform. That's what a two-sided network looks like in its early innings.
7/ Now add the biomarker loop. Generic peptides arrive on the same rails. The dataset deepens. The AI gets better at designing the right intervention for each person. Eventually pharma isn't just selling through $HIMS. It's building for it.

Just as $PLTR became the operating system for enterprise decisions, $HIMS is becoming the operating system where medicine meets the patient.
The molecule becomes the output. The platform that matches it to each human becomes the asset.

$DUOL is on track to become the world’s dominant superhuman personal AI tutor. It will outperform any human teacher on Earth, run at a fraction of the cost, and become the platform the rest of the education market builds on top of.

Q3 2026 just confirmed the engine is working. Here’s the chain:

1/ More learners. Duolingo averaged 64.9M daily active users in Q3, up 29% year over year. That’s the second straight quarter of acceleration. The “AI kills language apps” bear case needed DAU growth to keep falling. Instead it bottomed at 21% in Q1 and is heading back towards 30%.

2/ Record net adds, against seasonality. Duolingo added 6.2M DAUs in a quarter that is usually its weakest, roughly double a typical Q3. Users aren’t leaving for chatbots. They’re coming to the product that already turns AI into daily learning.

3/ Every learner becomes a source of learning-outcome data. Every lesson, every mistake, every streak, every before-and-after across millions of people, every single day. That is data no general-purpose LLM can access, and it compounds with every new user.

4/ The data makes the tutor better. Better prediction of what each person needs next, at lower cost per lesson. Better outcomes attract more learners. More learners generate more data. Every new customer makes the tutor smarter, and every improvement in the tutor attracts more customers.

5/ Monetization follows the users. Subscription bookings growth went from 10% to 16% in a single quarter. Users lead, bookings follow, and revenue follows bookings with a lag. The market priced the lagging indicator and missed the leading one.

6/ The cash is already compounding. LTM free cash flow per share went from $0.2 in Q4 2021 to $8.3 today, on $1.18B of LTM revenue. This isn’t a speculative AI story waiting for a business model. It’s a cash machine funding its own superintelligence.

7/ Eventually the tutor becomes superhuman. It’s personalised to every learner, patient at 3am, fluent in every subject, and it runs at a fraction of the cost of a human. The best private tutor on Earth used to be a luxury for a few thousand families. Duolingo is turning it into a subscription for hundreds of millions.

8/ Then the market inverts. Schools, tutoring firms, edtech apps and employers stop competing with the tutor and start building on top of it. If you don’t own the AI trained on the largest dataset of human learning outcomes, you depend on whoever does.

Just as $PLTR became the operating system for decisions, $DUOL becomes the operating system for learning.

The molecule was the output in healthcare. Here, the lesson is the output.

The intelligence that designs it becomes the asset.

Peptides moving towards approval is the first domino in a chain that ends with $HIMS worth $2,000 per share intrinsically by 2030. Here’s the chain:

2/ They ask it on the platform that already serves them. $HIMS is one of the largest D2C healthcare platforms on Earth, with a vertically integrated supply chain. Vertical integration wins on price. Price wins the customer.

3/ Every customer becomes a source of biomarker data. More patients, more panels, more longitudinal measurements, more before-and-after pairs. The dataset gets deeper every year.

4/ The AI gets smarter: better prediction, lower cost, better outcomes. Better outcomes attract more users. More users generate more data. Every new customer makes the machine smarter, and every improvement in the machine attracts more customers.

5/ Eventually the dataset is exhaustive enough that $HIMS AI can design personalised peptides for virtually anyone. Healthcare stops being about prescribing the same molecule to millions of people. It becomes about designing the optimal intervention for each individual, at a fraction of the cost of competing solutions.

6/ This unlocks an entirely new AI scaling law: life extension per token. It turns the pharmaceutical industry upside down. Traditional drug discovery becomes increasingly obsolete as value migrates to the AI trained on the largest, deepest, highest-quality longitudinal biomarker dataset.

7/ Everyone races to build or access that intelligence. If you don’t own it, you depend on it. Pharma suppliers depend on it because competitors using it design better interventions at lower cost. Customers depend on it because people using it may achieve better health outcomes and live longer than those who don’t.

8/ $HIMS becomes the most valuable subscription service on Earth as its AI grows increasingly predictive. Operating without $PLTR increasingly resembles operating without electricity. Except this time, the output isn’t productivity or economic efficiency.

It’s additional years of human life.

$AAOI earnings:

- $1B-$1.5B LTA disclosed with a hyperscaler customer

- 2nd LTA coming soon, worth 5x+ more (implying $5B-$7.5B), in its final stages.

This LTA explicitly includes lasers, very material for AOI that they're moving to supplying merchant lasers.

- "The demand is exceptional, unprecedented. I do not know what kind of superlatives to use to describe the amount of demand that we are seeing out there in the industry"

Yeah this commentary doesn't sound like any optical demand would slowed down if it's "exceptional + unprecedented"

- Rejected hyperscaler slowdowns from political changes with little effect.

- AOI Can only meet 80% of demand, in case there's a kind of reduction, the demand would be bigger than AOI future capacity

- Moving toward other financing methods than ATMs (thank god), US bank loans similar to what $NBIS is doing, I'd argue is positive, given FCF coming in later.

- Delay in meeting capacity projections into H1 2027. $471m/month targets pushed back into H2 2027, due to electrical procurement and construction logistics, which existed before Texas governor changed.

This part is negative part of the earnings call. To qualify this, I don't quite think hyperscalers would sign a $5-$7.5B LTA if they didn't think AOI couldn't deliver.

- Near term Q4 guidance cut was DSP availability. AOI revised near term projections down slightly to $385M and $420M in revenue.

Said DSP supply would ease early 2027 and that they're qualifying more suppliers.

- Gave hiked H2 2027 capacity projections from their expansion, near term revision downward.

- 4 to 5 ongoing UHP laser eval/quals for CPO

UHP laser segment alone would far outweigh their $3.8B MC, especially if you're executing on multi billion dollar contracts with 60%+ gross margin laseres.

TLDR:
- Long term visibility improved a lot, with est. $6-$9B cumulative LTA contracts coming soon.
- Shift toward supplying CPO lasers merchant is fundamentally material vs. just transceivers, and what I wanted to hear

$PLTR Must read ‼️ | “I don’t want to be particular to a certain vendor — but I will tell you, in the Maven Smart System Palantir Ontology — the reason JDPAC actually was the first in Transcom to use it was the power of it.”

In an exclusive interview with Ryan Samuelson, new light is shed on Transcom’s use of AI and the Maven Smart System (@PalantirTech) to accelerate strategic decision-making and data-sharing over the course of the Iran war.
______________________________________

“GRAPEVINE, Texas — Data scientists and other technical specialists were embedded next to uniformed military personnel inside U.S. Transportation Command’s global operations center for the first time during Operation Epic Fury to rapidly prototype AI-enabled tools in support of real-world warfare needs.

Those experts generated roughly “33 apps in just the first two weeks alone of OEF,” Transcom’s Chief Data and AI Officer Ryan Samuelson told DefenseScoop.”
…
“Transcom is known as an influential early adopter of Palantir’s Maven Smart System in the U.S. military enterprise. That operational AI and data-fusion software platform grew out of the Defense Department’s Project Maven, which launched nearly a decade ago.

MSS pulls disparate real-time data streams — such as satellite imagery, sensor telemetry, radar, flight paths, ship trackers and classified intelligence — into a single interface and uses computer vision and automated detection models to identify, track, and categorize potential military targets and other assets of interest.

“I don’t want to be particular to a certain vendor — but I will tell you, in the Maven Smart System Palantir Ontology — the reason JDPAC actually was the first in Transcom to use it was the power of it. What we realized is there’s not much else, at least right now, on the market that has the ontology to be able to put in the data, to be able to put in the apps, to have the secure development. It is the most powerful tool,” Samuelson said. “The ability to operate within that, to be able to share, is really, really powerful.”
…
“Samuelson said he tasked his team to deliver a minimum viable product within 24 hours, gather feedback, and continuously iterate to refine their tools. Everything was connected and deployed in MSS, and the team generated dozens of digital apps and dashboards.”
…
““We ended up taking the tool and all of the data that we dumped in Maven Smart System — when planes are moving, what the cargo flows were, all of that — and over a 24-hour period, our bot would look at all of that. And then [Transcom Commander Gen. Randall Reed] could come in every morning and go, ‘What happened in the last 24 hours?’ And in a matter of about 15 seconds, it would spit out a summary of, ‘This is your movements. Here’s how many were late, et cetera, et cetera,’” Samuelson said. “That used to take a team of probably four to five people hours to kind of curate that and give that [analysis].””

“When asked what commercial frontier AI models supported the work, he told DefenseScoop that the team used Palantir’s AI Hivemind product in MSS, which orchestrates, trains and re-trains AI agents…. We could easily say, ‘Hey, I now want you to take on this persona,’ or ‘I now want you to also add this” Samuelson said
…

“If we want to work at the speed of war, then we need to be able to see that constantly and fine tune our processes and day to day, so we can rapidly scale to war and we are better integrated,” the Transcom CDAO told DefenseScoop.

Paradis@ParadisLabs
07:22 SGTInvesting
On market crashes like today, I'm reminded of a piece of advice I got from a CIO mentor that traded during the dotcom and 08 crashes and lived to tell the tale.

He said: "Treat investing the same way you treat life."

That's all. It has stuck with me for many years because after filling in the blanks, you're forced to become "better" in both portfolio management and life management. It's uncanny how correlated they are.

Strip either one down and you're left with the same raw materials: time and uncertainty.

Every investment gives up something certain today for something uncertain tomorrow. So does nearly everything that matters in life. Love, learning, raising a child, starting a new job. Anything.

Both reward patience, but only after testing it.
You can't generate performance without risking losses, the same way you can't love without risking grief.

But fundamentally, the first rule of portfolio and life management is survival.
You can come back from most losses, but not from the one that takes you out of the game.

It's always darkest before the dawn.

22:17 SGTInvesting
The semis sell-off feels overcooked like McDonalds' chicken tenders.
I'm gently dipping my little toe back in the water today.

Positioning in AI stocks is now much cleaner thanks to last weeks de-leveraging. I view this as a good landscape to start adding risk...steadily.

The chart illustrates light positioning in their Prime Brokerage book, with Semis exposure back at July's Leopold lows (UBS).

Demand for AI remains robust and data centers will be built. Anthropic's October ARR number will be good. Yet current Semis and Mega Cap valuations have been heavily compressed which make no sense to me considering that EPS is expected to accelerate in 2027. We're essentially pricing-in a downcycle in 2028 rn? Won't Anthropic and other frontier labs continue filling their boots?? They've barely even started...

Using hyperscaler cloud backlog as a proxy, I'd say that AI fundamentals are in a good spot here. Midterm noise is largely behind us IMO and I don't see how the Democrats can risk AI leadership, consumer backlash AND ECONOMIC GROWTH for limited upside. The risk/reward seems heavily skewed to me.

JPM also raise a good point today - "Given how painful October was, hedge funds would not be in a hurry to start rebuilding their AI exposures before they see at least a few weeks of stability. In turn, a stability in AI stocks would require the support of retail investors. The latter will have to continue to buy the dip in AI stocks in November, as they did in October and as they have doing uninterruptedly since 2023. Some stability in November would then pave the way for hedge funds to start rebuilding their AI exposures from end-November onwards."

Makes sense. These guys are smarter than I am. But will HFs actually add AI exposure after the July AND October de-leveraging? So close to Year End too?? That's the near-term risk...

Stay safe!! 🍊

*My situation is not your situation. Let's put on our big boy pants and recognise that this is not tailored financial advice pls!
**Respect the flows! I am purposely choosing not to respect them!! Hyperscalers up, Semis down today is a continuance from yesterday's post-Midterm flows!!!
***I personally see further downside before HFs start adding risk EOY. Significant hurdles ahead incl. Iran and Anthropic's IPO. Not calling any bottoms here but eventually you just gotta buy something exciting lol.

Here’s an app I’ve been working on - built entirely with @bot and @build.

A stock screener app built exactly how I like it: Straight to the point with the information I care about readily available for vetting stock prospects. Hence, I named it “Bottom Line”. Nearly all the data in the app is directly pulled from the SEC.

One of my favorite features is how the landing page of a company profile immediately flags items such as a high burn rate relative to cash, insider sell clusters, etc. I also really like the insider activity tab that lets me see immediately whether an insider sale was pre-planned or not.

I currently pay $10/mo for a similar service, except I like my version much more. I will be cancelling that subscription and start using Bottom Line as my main.

I’m still working on refining it but plan on posting the link to the app once I’m done. What’s cool is that you can save it to your home screen and access it just like any other app on your phone.
